title: n11 class2-lane raw-batch integrity audit + cost-69b line-wrap corruption repair
auditor: long-term lane session 9 (remote-only audit while execution env unavailable)
finding: cost-69b raw batch files B, C, D each contained one JSON row broken across two physical lines mid-token (bit 32 in B at 'termi|nalStoneRange', bit 86 in C at 'ter|minalStoneRange', bit 110 in D at 'capped|,fal'... pattern: hard line wrap inserted mid-string). As pushed, strict JSONL parsers recovered only 66/69 candidate rows (sum 292,561,827); the sweep record claims 69 rows / 305,754,861 nodes.
repair: The 3 broken rows were reconstructed by rejoining each fragment pair; all field values were preserved verbatim (only the spurious line break was removed). After repair: 69 unique candidate rows, node sum exactly 305,754,861 == sweep record total_nodes, 0 capped, 0 WIN7 (bit rows all loss=false), 4/4 pilots at 5,949 nodes. The corrupted B/C/D files are overwritten in place with the repaired versions; batch A was intact.

lesson: Raw JSONL pushes must be verified with a strict per-line JSON.parse pass over the fetched remote content; a file that merely looks well-formed locally can acquire hard wraps in transport. All future raw batch pushes should include a remote line-parse receipt.
